1) Please confirm the hard RTO/RPO targets for a full region failover vs. a partial (single-availability-zone) degradation. Do you offer tiered commitments or a single SLA?

3) What are the operational prerequisites on our side for a <15 minute failover (DNS TTLs, routing propagation, pre-warmed model cache, network ACLs you cannot change)?

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; attached is a concise runbook extract and a tiering spreadsheet that maps commitment levels to operational prerequisites.

Attachments: (attachment: redwood-safe-failover-runbook.pdf - 980KB, application/pdf)
             (attachment: rto-rpo-tiering-appendix.xlsx - 120KB, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Summary commitments (customer-facing):
- Multi-region full failover (Managed Dedicated or Private deployments): we offer configurable tiers. Standard Tier: RTO ≤ 15 minutes, RPO ≤ 5 minutes. FastFail Tier (reserved capacity + warmed caches + pre-defined routing): RTO ≤ 2 minutes, RPO ≤ 1 minute. BestEffort Tier: RTO ≤ 60 minutes, RPO ≤ 15 minutes.

- Partial/AZ-level degradations: Default behaviour is degraded throughput with automatic request routing to healthy AZs; there is no data loss for fully committed writes once acknowledged. RPO for AZ-level fallback is typically ≤ 1 minute depending on replication policy.

- Active-active opt-in: For customers who enable active-active across regions we provide near-synchronous replication for customer state via our WAL-backed streaming layer (configurable). When enabled and tested, this supports RPO ≤ 1 minute in practice; RPO=0 (zero data loss) is only achievable with customer-managed synchronous replication patterns — we can support and document the steps but cannot guarantee zero for all workloads without those patterns.

Operational prerequisites for sub-15 minute failover (what we need from Novacorp):
- DNS TTLs ≤ 60s or use route53 weighted policies with pre-warmed endpoints.
- Reserved FastFail capacity configured and model images pre-pulled in target region.
- Network ACLs and VPC peering/firewall rules pre-authorised for both primary and secondary regions.
- Warmed KV caches per rollout (we provide a cache-warming API and a warmed snapshot can be staged during runbook rehearsals).
- Test window scheduled with our runbook run-through (we recommend one rehearsal before go-live).

Limitations & caveats:
- In-flight requests during the narrow window of a sudden network partition may require client-side retry logic to achieve perceived zero loss.
- For PCI/regulated write-ahead requirements we recommend our FastFail Tier plus synchronous replication of the write stream to customer-managed sinks.

Next steps: If this looks acceptable I can schedule a 60-min technical runbook walk-through with your DR committee; Jordan and Grace are copied for technical sequencing.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability

Subject: Re: Clarification on activation windows and RTO/RPO for multi-site failover — consolidated commitments and next steps

Hi Laura — consolidated responses below; Jordan and Grace have reviewed and signed off. We also attached a procurement-ready SLA paragraph and an Exhibit A credit table.

Consolidated commitments (FastFail Tier — conditions required):
- Operational commitment: RTO ≤ 2 minutes (failover start = activation signal or detection alert; end = 95% 200 OK over 60s sample)
- RPO: ≤ 30 seconds for write-ahead/transaction streams when the customer enables WAL streaming to our durable stream (or mirrors to a customer-managed sink) and reserves FastFail capacity in the failover region.
- For AZ-level incidents: RPO ≤ 1 minute (replication-on-write by default).

Procurement language excerpt (for insertion into MSA):
"Failover measurement and credits: Failover start is recorded at the earlier of (i) Customer activation request; or (ii) Redwood automated region-unavailable detection. Failover end is recorded when 95% of sampled requests to the Customer-configured endpoint return 200 OK over a contiguous 60-second window. If Redwood fails to meet the RTO described in the chosen tier, Customer is eligible for service credits as set forth in Exhibit A. Exhibit A defines credit amounts escalating by the percentage deviation from the RTO commitment."

Telemetry & rehearsals:
- We will provide a rehearsal telemetry bundle including request/response latency histograms, model-load timing, cache-warm success/failure logs, and optional packet timing captures for the rehearsal window.
- We will run one joint rehearsal with your DR committee prior to go-live; additional rehearsals can be scheduled and will be documented.

Operational prerequisites (recap):
- DNS TTL ≤ 60s OR pre-configured weighted routing with our endpoints pre-registered.
- Reserved FastFail capacity and pre-pulled model images in the secondary region.
- Network ACLs/VPC peering in place for both regions.
- Customer enables WAL streaming or mirrors writes if zero/near-zero RPO is required.

Next steps:
1) Accept the attached Exhibit A credit table and SLA paragraph (attachment: Exhibit-A-sla-credits.pdf).
2) Schedule a 60-min runbook walk-through with your DR committee (proposed slots attached).
3) Confirm FastFail capacity reservation (we will provision a temporary 48-hour reservation for your rehearsal if you confirm the slot).

We can convert the commitment language above into a short contractual amendment for the MSA once procurement confirms the Exhibit A selection. Let me know which day/time works for the runbook walk-through and I’ll send calendar invites.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
